So there's now a test folder where they write messages by hand under the proposed rules. Claude has sent Codex the first question: does it read Codex's review the same way? Waiting on Codex.

The first test found a flaw. Records written in the same second came out in a random order. A fix was patched into the folder's rules. The real tool still needs ids that always go up, and the agreement needs an ordering rule for two writers.

attributes.summary: Claude and Codex need one written agreement on how the shared mailbox works before either builds anything. Claude has drafted it from the plan, Codex's review and the hand test. Codex hasn't reviewed it yet, and Al hasn't accepted it. Four questions are still open.

Codex showed that waiting a few seconds can't settle who a message is for. The draft agreement now uses a short lock and a numbered registry version stamped on each message. Not settled until the agreement is accepted.

Codex joined late, caught up and agreed with most of the model. Claude took Codex's ordering fix and its two findings into the folder's rules. Claude replied and asked Codex to review the draft agreement.

The ordering problem now has a full answer in the draft. Every record gets a number from one counter while a lock is held. Not settled until the agreement is accepted.

attributes.text: Al wanted Claude and Codex on a real mailbox quickly, without building things nobody needs yet. So only the hand-run first slice is approved. The automatic relay, the router and the session skills stay as drafts until real use shows they're needed.

attributes.summary: Recorded what the first slice covers and what it leaves out, so the rest of the plan is clearly still to do.

All 11 checks pass against throwaway mailboxes. They cover sending, replying the right way, late joiners catching up, one person finishing without hiding mail from another, many writers at once, and recovery after a crash.

Claude and Codex now have a real shared mailbox on this Mac, and a command to use it by hand. The real channel is set up, and a welcome message is waiting for Codex. Not done: the first real round trip with Codex, plus roles, hand-overs and retries.
Codex said draft 3 is ready for first use and asked to move onto a real mailbox. The agreement now has a working first version behind it. Al's formal review of the agreement itself is still to come.
